content.problemStatement:
With a Tic-Tac-Toe board as a string array `board`, output `true` exactly when it is possible to reach this board position during the course of a valid tic-tac-toe game.

The board is a `3 x 3` array that is composed of characters `' '`, `'X'`, and `'O'`. The `' '` character represents an empty square.

Here are the rules of Tic-Tac-Toe:

* Players take turns placing characters into empty squares `' '`.
* The first player always places `'X'` characters, while the second player always places `'O'` characters.
* `'X'` and `'O'` characters are always placed into empty squares, never filled ones.
* The game ends when there are three of the same (non-empty) character filling any row, column, or diagonal.
* The game also ends if all squares are non-empty.
* No more moves can be played if the game is over.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/05/15/tictactoe1-grid.jpg)

```
Input: board = ["O  ","   ","   "]
Output: false
Explanation: The first player always plays "X".
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/05/15/tictactoe2-grid.jpg)

```
Input: board = ["XOX"," X ","   "]
Output: false
Explanation: Players take turns making moves.
```

**Example 3:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/05/15/tictactoe4-grid.jpg)

```
Input: board = ["XOX","O O","XOX"]
Output: true
```

**Constraints:**

* `board.length == 3`
* `board[i].length == 3`
* `board[i][j]` is either `'X'`, `'O'`, or `' '`.

notes: The reference algorithm is constant-time for the fixed 3 x 3 board.

The count invariant is O's count equal to X's count or one less.
A winning player must have made the move that ends the game, so its count determines which player could have just moved.
Checking all rows, columns, and diagonals is constant work for a 3 x 3 board.
solution.approach: Count X and O, verify that turns alternate, then check all eight possible winning lines. A winning X position is valid only when X has one more move than O; a winning O position is valid only when both counts are equal. These conditions also reject positions where play continued after a win or where both players have winning lines.

better.complexity: Exponential in the number of cells; bounded for this problem but not needed for the production solution.
better.description: Generate reachable states with recursive backtracking while pruning as soon as a win occurs. This avoids exploring moves that could only happen after the game has already ended, but it still performs substantially more work than necessary for a fixed 3 x 3 board.

optimal.complexity: O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: Use two invariants. First, legal alternating play requires count(O) == count(X) or count(O) == count(X)-1. Second, if X has a winning line, X must have exactly one more move than O; if O has a winning line, their counts must be equal. If both players win, these conditions cannot both hold, so the state is rejected. With a fixed 3 x 3 board, all checks take constant time.

bruteForce.complexity: O(9!) time in the worst case and O(R) space for the reachable-state set, where R is the number of stored states.
bruteForce.description: Enumerate legal move sequences from the empty board, stopping immediately when a player wins or the board becomes full. Record every reachable board and test whether the input board is among them. This is straightforward but explores many move orders unnecessarily.

solution.timeComplexity: O(1), because the board always contains exactly 9 cells.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1), using only counters and a constant number of boolean flags.
